entry.title: VS Code v1_146: Trust and security
entry.summary: Improved permission prompts The Copilot harness previously suggested overly broad tool-level allowances for operations like web fetches, terminal commands, and file reads. For example, the default action for fetching a URL was "Allow in this Session", which would let the model access any URL during that session. Now, permission prompts are more granular, by default adding allowances for specific domains, commands, and directories.

Organization help links for policy restrictions

entry.title: VS Code v1_146: Chat
entry.summary: Continue a Copilot CLI session in VS Code (Experimental) When you're working with theGitHub Copilot CLIin a terminal outside VS Code, you can now move the session into VS Code and keep going. Enter/codein the CLI, or/code-insidersfor VS Code Insiders. The CLI exits, and VS Code opens the same session in the Chat view of the window for the session's folder, starting VS Code if it isn't running. The session keeps its conversation history, its model and reasoning effort, and its mode and permission
